item.statement: The authors note that the alloy exhibits low ductility and undergoes intergranular fracture, indicating a trade-off between the achieved ultra-high strength and plasticity.
quotes: The SPS–processed CoCrFeNiTi HEA underwent intergranular fracture.
Additionally, the regions of deformation are marked by arrows, which confirms that nanoprecipitates play an important role in high strength and low ductility.
High–entropy alloys (HEAs) with body–centered cubic (BCC) structures are renowned for their remarkable strength, yet they lack the flexibility inherent in other alloy types.

item.statement: The paper observes that while higher sintering temperatures improve density, lower temperatures result in significant porosity due to suppressed atomic diffusion.
quotes: When the sintering temperature is 950 °C, the measured density of the alloy is much lower than the theoretical density with 6.57 g/cm 3 .
Due to the suppression of atomic diffusion at low temperatures, there is a decrease in the interaction between powder particles during the sintering process.
As the sintering temperature increases from 1000 °C to 1050 °C, the density of the alloy increases from 6.73 g/cm 3 to 6.98 g/cm 3 , further approaching the theoretical value.

item.statement: The study highlights a trade-off where increasing milling time improves hardness through grain refinement but also increases internal strain and cold working effects.
quotes: The hardness values exhibited an increasing trend according to increasing milling time.
This increasing in hardness resulted from grain refinement and enhanced dislocation density due to prolonged milling.
The intense collisions during the process induced significant cold working and work hardening effects in the particles, leading to a decrease in the average particle size.
